what: Manulife Financial is a Canadian insurer. It sells life and health insurance and manages retirement money in Canada, the United States under the John Hancock brand, and across Asia, where it has one of the largest footprints of any Western insurer.
customers: Individuals buying life, health and retirement products, and institutions using its asset management arm.
money: life and health insurance in Hong Kong, Japan and Southeast Asia
life insurance and long-term care policies
moat: Distribution agreements and agent networks in Asian markets that took decades to build, and the scale to carry long-dated insurance risk.
risks: Legacy US long-term care policies have needed repeated reserve increases
Insurance accounting makes reported revenue volatile and hard to read
Interest rate moves change the value of long-dated liabilities
Analyst coverage in this data is thin and the single target implies downside
opportunities: Asian insurance sales grow faster than in developed markets
Reinsurance deals have removed some legacy long-term care risk
Fee income from wealth management is capital-light
watch: Asian new business value and long-term care reserve assumptions.
